decisions.summary: Row 215 (_canal_ft#canal narrows at each offtake) held and re-tiered E2 -> E3 on measure instead of working the five newly refused layouts in this wave
decisions.why: The spec's Edge Case 'A fix that changes many maps' provides exactly this route: where making the failing maps pass takes more work than the row's tier, the row takes that work's tier. Five seeds refused by four different rules (row_rules, web needle loops, the brook rule, water_rules) is a change across modules, FR-003's E3. Re-tiering by measured work is the request's own ordering ('rank by how much implementation work... go from easiest to hardest'); the row stays in the ranking, kept in scope, to be fixed in tier order. Same route as the accepted holds of the garden flank (wave 60) and the privy seats (wave 62).

decisions.summary: The re-tiered row itself carries the layouts' work (its fix names them, after: []) rather than a separate found row
decisions.why: The layouts' breakage is the row's own fix's work, not a separate departure from research; the accepted precedents (ranking rows for wave 60 and 62) record it the same way.
0069 settles what the implementation should be (the square-root law, frame.taper_w); the open work is placement, not research. FR-003.
